answers.text: Have it return the same three-line shape every time — date, item/quantity, then change. The date line is just the date, the item line is item plus quantity, the third is the change or 'no change'.
Get it to list every claim on its own line with date, amount, category and submitter, then a total. Say the total has to be the sum of every amount, not just typed in.
Something in the dates here doesn't add up. The email says the 19th is three days from today, but the call it references was the 14th, five days off.
The 62 versus 54 works out to about 15%, so that bit's fine. But 3 late out of 62 works out closer to 95%, not the 97% it says.
Output 2's the one I'd approve, it doesn't just give a number. Output 1 doesn't say what the actual sales or returns figures were.
Reply 2's the one I'd send as-is, it names the order and the credit. There's nothing behind Reply 1's claim that it was all our fault.

1. No.
2. Yes, that's fine.
3. No, not that one.
4. Yes, that one's fine.
5. No, that one stays out.
I'd hold back the unit pricing and discounts rather than paste them straight in. The confidentiality clause names both companies, so I'd be careful with that part too.
I'd add a step where someone checks the totals against the system before it goes out. It happens just before the report is sent up, not at some point earlier.
The extraction step is where things could first go wrong, before anything downstream sees it. Step 4 is the one that needs a gate, since that's when the email sends with no one looking.
